name: Nongkhnum River Island
description: Largest river island in Meghalaya (about 21 sq km), formed by the bifurcation of the Kynshi River into Phanliang and Namliang branches. Features sandy beaches, clear waters, and nearby waterfalls; often promoted as Asia’s second-largest river island. Quiet picnic, camping and nature spot near Nongstoin.
facts: Located about 14 km from Nongstoin, HQ of West Khasi Hills
Area approximately 21 km²; formed by Kynshi River split
Contains or adjacent to Weinia Falls and views of Langshiang Falls
Low tourist infrastructure; ideal for peaceful nature visits

name: Shillong
description: Capital of Meghalaya and headquarters of East Khasi Hills, a popular hill station at about 1,500 m elevation. Known as the Scotland of the East for its pine-clad hills, colonial architecture, educational institutions, and scenic surroundings.
facts: Gateway to Cherrapunji and other Khasi Hills attractions
Features Police Bazaar, golf course, and many parks

name: Shillong Peak
description: Highest point in Meghalaya at approximately 1,965 m, about 10 km south of Shillong. Offers panoramic views of the city, surrounding hills, and on clear days the Bangladesh plains. Sacred to Khasi people as dwelling of U Lei Shillong.
facts: Requires photo ID for entry due to Air Force station

name: Elephant Falls
description: Popular three-tiered waterfall in Upper Shillong, East Khasi Hills. Locally known as Ka Kshaid Lai Pateng Khohsiew. Easily accessible with stairs to viewing points amid lush greenery and ferns.
facts: About 12 km from Shillong city center
Named after a former elephant-shaped rock

name: Ward's Lake
description: Historic artificial horseshoe-shaped lake in the heart of Shillong, also known as Pollock Lake or Nan Polok. Surrounded by botanical gardens, with a wooden bridge, boating, and flower beds.

name: Sohra (Cherrapunji)
description: Iconic town in East Khasi Hills, once known as the wettest place on Earth. Famous for dramatic waterfalls, living root bridges, limestone caves, and misty plateaus overlooking Bangladesh plains.
facts: Record rainfall of over 26,000 mm in 1861
Gateway to Nohkalikai, living root bridges, and caves

name: Nohkalikai Falls
description: Tallest plunge waterfall in India at about 340 m, near Sohra. Dramatic single drop into a turquoise pool at the base of the escarpment, with local legend of Ka Likai.
facts: Named after the legend of Likai

name: Nohsngithiang Falls (Seven Sisters)
description: Segmented waterfall near Mawsmai, also called Seven Sisters Falls. Multiple streams cascade over the cliff edge, especially impressive during monsoon, with views toward Bangladesh plains.
facts: Best in rainy season when multiple streams flow

name: Mawsmai Cave
description: Lit limestone show cave near Sohra, about 150 m of accessible passages with stalactites and stalagmites. Easy for most visitors with some narrow sections.
facts: One of the most accessible caves in Meghalaya

name: Double Decker Living Root Bridge (Nongriat)
description: Iconic two-tier living root bridge grown from Ficus elastica roots by Khasi people over generations in Nongriat village. Requires a steep trek of about 3,500 steps from Tyrna.
facts: Part of UNESCO tentative listing for living root bridges

name: Mawlynnong Village
description: Famous as Asia's cleanest village, in Pynursla block near the Bangladesh border. Features neat homes, living root bridge at nearby Riwai, balancing rock, and community-managed cleanliness.
facts: Declared cleanest village in Asia in 2003
Living root bridge and balancing rock nearby

name: Laitlum Canyon
description: Dramatic viewpoint and canyon near Smit, about 25 km from Shillong. Offers sweeping views of deep green valleys and ridges, with steep steps leading down into the gorge.
facts: About 25 km from Shillong via Smit

name: Mawphlang Sacred Forest
description: Ancient sacred grove (Law Lyngdoh) protected by Khasi traditions for centuries. Biodiversity-rich primary forest about 25 km from Shillong; visitors must take nothing from the forest.
facts: Protected by local beliefs for centuries

name: Arwah Cave
description: Limestone cave near Sohra known for fossilized remains in the walls, including shells and bones. More spacious than Mawsmai with a short forest approach.
facts: Often combined with other Sohra attractions

name: Kongthong Village
description: Remote village in East Khasi Hills known as the Whistling Village, where residents use unique whistled tunes as names and for communication. Features living root bridges and traditional Khasi culture.
facts: Living root bridges in the vicinity

name: Don Bosco Centre for Indigenous Cultures
description: Major museum in Shillong showcasing the cultures, lifestyles, and artifacts of indigenous peoples of Northeast India across multiple galleries.
facts: One of the finest museums on Northeast indigenous cultures
